flags.summary: In-house instalment plan quoted at six payments with an extra $200 per month described as processing fees, taking a $6,000 offer to $7,200 — a 20% uplift on a plan the prospect was actively considering.
evidence: We, there's a few things we can do from what I'm hearing. So we can do that. We for now split up into six payments in house, basically, that would come with an extra $200 a month for processing fees, etc.

when it comes to in-house, like, the maximum we could do is that we split up over six months, and then if you feel like after, like, next month, your new venture blows up, and you feel like, hey, I just want to pay it all off right now, we can still do that, and then the rest of, like, those 200 extra per month, that would just go completely away
I wasn't expecting to drop an extra thousand bucks a month right now.

flags.summary: Rep improvised a first-month cancellation option that forms no part of the six-month offer, after having stated that terms are not set and vary by personal situation; the prospect confirmed it would move his decision.
evidence: The only thing I can then think of that would actually maybe make it better for your situation is usually when we start a payment plan, let's say, it's every month it just gets paid, but we also have a [try] it or leave it, I would say. And that's where we could get started.

And if you don't feel like after our moms are going with my business, it's not going like the way I want it to go. And you don't really see the results, you don't really see the benefits, we can stop it. But with the idea to continue for the rest of the five months, and that would just be the first monthly payment.
It's just that we don't have anything set in stone. Like, this is exactly what we can split it up with. It comes down to the personal situation, basically.
That's good. And that will help me make a decision to do it. And those two things would probably sway my decision

flags.summary: Prospect described a year of cascading back injuries requiring physiotherapy, said he may still be 'on thin ice', and reported active elbow connective-tissue soreness he expects to fail if he keeps progressing; he was moved toward progressive loaded kettlebell training with no clinician clearance sought.
evidence: I picked up my son was holding him like this and put him in the crib and the whole middle back went out. I went to physio and then, you know, this part of the back went out and then the neck and shoulders went out. So kind of like over a year of like physio
But who knows if I'm on thin ice there, but I've kind of fixed that and it worked and it's better, but I don't know if there's, if it's still thin ice

the one spot where I feel maybe some weaknesses coming is, is right in this area here, because I can feel a little bit of soreness... It's more so on the connective tissue around it. I feel like that could be one thing that goes if I continue this progression.
do you feel like there's anything internally for you that would stop you? — Honestly, just an injury at this point
because your back went out in the past and also with the left elbow issue, Trevor is going to make a specific mobility program for you as well

flags.summary: Asked a direct physiological question about the hormonal effects of extended calorie deficits, the rep gave an unqualified opinion rather than deferring it to the coach.
evidence: I'm reading stuff that like you should only cut for six months max you don't want to affect your hormones you know like how true is that

to sort of point that out with cutting sometimes you want to go a little bit longer even though that might outbalance your hormones for a short time because if we go back to maintenance it's going to take even longer for us to cut down and then we still going to have that effect eventually so just a small pointer there

flags.summary: No written description of the six-month programme exists; asked for anything documenting what $6,000 buys, the rep confirmed there is nothing to send.
evidence: You've outlined what you get, but if you have a white paper or a PDF of what's included for the six months, maybe even a schedule or something, that would be... I know you're not giving programs or anything like that, but just an idea.
Actually, we don't really have it written out, to be honest. Basically, how it's gone, I've become completely trained, of course, on what we specifically have, and it's all in here.
Like I said, I don't have anything to send over to you as I'm like, this is exactly what we do.

flags.summary: Rep gave an absolute outcome assurance alongside a loosely stated continue-until-results guarantee, leaving the terms and limits of both undefined.
evidence: if you do everything correctly, like how you should be doing it, and we haven't seen the progress of at least getting to being more ripped right and having that longevity aspect for yourself, then Trevor does continue coaching you. But I'm like 99% sure that that's not going to happen because you are dedicated and Trevor knows his stuff.

If we don't get the results, even though they have 100% put in the effort, then we'll continue coaching them until they get the results, but because it seems like you're dedicated, you have that new identity for yourself, it's going to be six months and we are 100% going to go past your goals.
